_about: Tunable numbers, skip rules and prompts for scripts/governance/doc-clarity-guard.py (records saves) and doc-clarity-gate.py (blocks). Spec: docs/plans/harness/doc-clarity-guard/spec-gate.md.

codes._about: Part C bare-code check. regex matches short ids like B4, A5a-04, S-39, REQ-B7.

gate.reader_prompt:
You check one document that an AI assistant wrote. First decide if it is a report for the owner. The owner is a busy product manager, not an engineer. They read it once, between meetings, with zero context: they never saw the assistant's code, files, plans, agents or audit notes. Their rule: a smart 18-year-old must understand every sentence on the first read.
Set is_owner_report to false for build specs, designs, task files, test fixtures, code docs, logs and other notes written for agents or engineers. Then return verdict PASS and no problems.
If it is a report, a review, an audit, a plan or a recommendation for the owner, find the places where the owner would have to stop and ask "what does this mean?":
1. A code, ID, short name or made-up project word (for example "B4", "stagger", "the gap floor", "fastStore", "lane lean") used in prose without a plain explanation right there. A glossary at the top does not count for a term used much later. IDs kept only in a table column for lookup are fine.
2. A sentence that only makes sense if you already know the system (it leans on unseen files, earlier runs, or internal steps).
3. A table cell that is a bare fragment the owner cannot decode.
4. A finding with no plain statement of what to do about it.
5. A recommendation with no gain and no cost stated.
6. A decision for the owner with no options, or with no recommendation.
Do NOT flag: file paths, command names or code shown in backticks as a label; everyday business or product words; one or two minor side terms that do not block the main point; length.
BLOCK when the owner could not follow the main points on a first read, or when there are 5 or more distinct places. Otherwise PASS. Most clear docs pass, even long ones.
Reply with JSON only: {"is_owner_report": true or false, "verdict": "PASS" or "BLOCK", "problems": [{"where": "<section heading>", "text": "<the exact words, at most 12>", "fix": "<what to explain, at most 15 words>"}]}. List at most 12 problems, worst first.
gate.recheck_prompt:
You re-check one document that an AI assistant rewrote for its owner, a busy product manager with zero context. Last time a reviewer listed the items below. Check ONLY these items. Do not look for other problems, except a new unexplained code or made-up word added in a rewritten sentence.
For each listed item: status FIXED if the owner can now follow that point on a first read (the term is explained in plain words where used, or the detail is gone), else OPEN. Copy where, text and fix from the list.
Put each new unexplained code or made-up word you find in "new".
Reply with JSON only: {"items": [{"where": "...", "text": "...", "fix": "...", "status": "FIXED" or "OPEN"}], "new": [{"where": "...", "text": "...", "fix": "..."}]}
gate.rewrite_message: Rewrite the doc so a smart 18-year-old with zero context understands every sentence on the first read. Keep every fact and number. Explain each term where it is used, or drop it. Then finish again.
gate.limit_message: {path} still fails the clarity check after {n} rewrites. Open items: {items}. In your final report, mark the state partial and name this doc and its open items.
gate.code_finding_fix: define each code in plain words where it is used, or move it to a reference column
